packages.label: אוֹר הַשֵּׁם וְהַכָּבוֹד
packages.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states: 'וְעִקַּר אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַכָּבוֹד' (line 4) — the essence of divine light IS kavod. This is the central bechina equivalence of the entire Torah. Later (line 5) the Rebbe repeats 'אֲזַי מְקַבֵּל אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁהוּא הַכָּבוֹד' — confirming the equation. The divine light and divine honor are two names for the same reality: the continuous divine flow that God pours out upon creation. This package also naturally absorbs שפע (divine abundance/flow), which the Rebbe mentions in line 3 ('אוֹר וְשֶׁפַע שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ') as the two aspects of the divine outpouring — light and shefa are treated as equivalent outflow terms in this Torah.

source_basis.bechina_type: explicit equivalence — 'the essence of X is Y'

source_basis.bechina_type: paired terms — light and shefa treated as co-referential

packages.label: חָכְמָה וְאַיִן — הַבִּיטּוּל
packages.reason: Three concepts cluster around the domain of self-nullification and its equation with chokhmah: (1) חכמה is explicitly equated with אין via the verse 'הַחָכְמָה מֵאַיִן תִּמָּצֵא' (Job 28:12, line 6) — wisdom is found from/in nothingness, meaning chokhmah IS ayin; (2) the wise (חכמים) are called 'אַיִן' directly: 'הַחֲכָמִים שֶׁהֵם אַיִן'; (3) the practice of ביטול עצמו / אינו כלל מזה העולם (lines 3 and 5) is the human expression of this same ayin-quality — the person who is nothing from this world embodies the chokhmah/ayin principle. All three are bechinas of the same underlying state: the nullified, physicality-free orientation that blocks nothing and receives everything. This is structurally independent from Package 1 (divine light/kavod) because chokhmah/bitul is the quality of the RECEIVER, while kavod/light is the quality of what is RECEIVED — they are related by eitza (nullification enables reception), not by shared nature.
nodes: ביטול עצמו / אינו כלל מזה העולם

source_basis.bechina_type: the practical form of the ayin-state; line 5 equates this with 'מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ'

packages.label: פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת — חַיִּים וָטוֹב
packages.label_en: The Joyful Face — Life and Good
packages.reason: Line 7 states: 'כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת – חַיִּים וְטוֹבָה לָעוֹלָם'. The showing of a joyful face IS life and good — this is an explicit bechina equation: פנים שוחקות = חיים וטובה. Line 8 confirms with the verse: 'רְאֵה נָתַתִּי לִפְנֵיכֶם הַיּוֹם אֶת הַחַיִּים וְאֶת הַטּוֹב... הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם' — life and good ARE the faces you show. The Rebbe also applies this to the tzaddik: 'וְכֵן הַצַּדִּיק, כְּשֶׁמַּרְאֶה פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת, הוּא טוֹב' — the tzaddik's joyful face = good. This package covers the positive pole of the face-domain. It is distinct from Package 1 (divine light/kavod) in that panim is the *mode of revelation* of kavod — the way the light reaches the world — rather than being the light itself.

source_basis.quote: כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַרְאֶה פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת – חַיִּים וְטוֹבָה לָעוֹלָם
source_basis.bechina_type: explicit equivalence — showing joyful face = life and good
'הַיְנוּ' = definitional bechina — life/good IS the panim

packages.label: פָּנִים זוֹעֲפוֹת — מָוֶת וָרָע
packages.label_en: The Averted Face — Death and Evil
packages.reason: The evil mirror of Package 3 is explicitly stated in the same verses. Line 7: 'וּלְהֵפֶךְ – לְהֵפֶךְ, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם' — the reverse face = the reverse outcome (death and evil). Line 8 cites 'אֶת הַמָּוֶת וְכוּ'' in the same 'הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם' formula — death/evil also IS the face shown. This is the structural evil mirror of Package 3 (the good face/life package): the same panim concept oriented negatively produces its opposite. The Rebbe applies this symmetry to God and to the tzaddik alike. Per the framework's good/evil mirror principle (§4), every good package has an exact evil counterpart — this is that counterpart for Package 3.

source_basis.bechina_type: mirror inversion — the negative face = the negative outcome

source_basis.quote: אֶת הַמָּוֶת וְכוּ', הַיְנוּ לַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּכֶם
source_basis.bechina_type: הַיְנוּ bechina — death is the averted/negative face

packages.label: גַּשְׁמִיּוּת וְהַצֵּל
packages.reason: Lines 2-3 establish a sustained metaphysical bechina: the shadow (צל) is caused by a physical/material thing (דָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי) standing opposite a spiritual/finer thing. The Rebbe gives three examples — wood and stone vs sunlight, earth's shadow causing eclipses, the sun itself relative to what is above it — all to establish that גשמיות (physicality/materiality) and צל (shadow) are the same reality: 'הָאָדָם כְּפִי גַּשְׁמִיּוּתוֹ... כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה צֵל'. This is a sustained bechina teaching: a person's degree of physicality IS their degree of shadow-casting. The Rebbe uses 'כְּפִי' (according to) throughout — the measure of physicality = the measure of shadow. מעשים רעים (evil deeds) are the third element: they are what increases/generates the גשמיות-צל. All three belong to the same domain: the negative material-obstacle realm. This is the evil/neutral blocking-mechanism cluster of Torah #172.

source_basis.quote: הַצֵּל הוּא מִדָּבָר גַּשְׁמִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד נֶגֶד דָּבָר רוּחָנִי
source_basis.bechina_type: definitional — shadow IS the physical standing against the spiritual

source_basis.quote: הָאָדָם כְּפִי גַּשְׁמִיּוּתוֹ וּכְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו, כֵּן עוֹשֶׂה צֵל
source_basis.bechina_type: proportional equivalence — physicality and evil deeds = shadow

stats.note_on_dataset_gap: This Torah is entirely absent from the bechina graph in torahData.js. All package structure is derived from the source text. The single existing edge (id=236, type='eitza') connects 'אם האדם מבטל עצמו ואינו כלל מזה העולם' to 'אינו עושה צל ומקבל אור השם יתברך' — this is correctly classified as eitza (the nullification PRODUCES the reception of light, it does not share the same nature as the light).
stats.torah_structure: The Torah's argument follows three moves: [Physical deeds → shadow that blocks light] →eitza→ [Nullification/ayin/chokhmah → no shadow] →eitza→ [Reception of divine light = kavod]. The face/panim section (lines 7-8) is a coda extending the light-kavod concept: the mode of kavod's appearance IS the face shown (good face = life, averted face = death). The good/evil mirror is fully present: Package 3 (joyful face/life) mirrors Package 4 (averted face/death); Package 2 (chokhmah/bitul) mirrors Package 5 (physicality/evil deeds/shadow) as the positive vs negative states of the human receiver.
